justification: Contribution is a formal model of what the failed attempt leaves in context across retries (clean-restart dominance); theorems are fitted to SWE-bench Verified traces in the lab, so validation not evaluation.
Contribution is postcondition verification and verify-before-retry gating each tool call; tested only in a simulated environment with injected faults, so lab validation.
Headline artefacts are a failure taxonomy plus AgentErrorBench of annotated failure trajectories and a debugging framework; evaluated on ALFWorld/GAIA/WebShop rollouts in the lab.
Contribution is turning attributed failure steps into minimal counterfactual repairs fed back at test time (revision, not the check); measured on four existing benchmarks in the lab.
Object is the compaction summary carrying killed-process output across sessions as truth; the paper reports a failure observed in the authors' own Claude Code use, with no study design.
Audits LLM-judges as acceptance monitors for false success and proposes lightweight detectors as the check; evidence is 9,876 tau2-bench and 1,879 AppWorld trajectories, a lab benchmark study.
Headline artefact is a fault-injection workbench for reproducing and comparing agent failures, not a loop mechanism; evidence is 120 scenarios with faults and mitigations deliberately varied.
Contributes SymTrace replay framework and the SymFail failure dataset as instruments for judging MAS repair methods; repairs compared under recorded-trace interventions in the lab.
Contribution is runtime restructuring of team topology (factorising an overloaded agent, hot-swapping it to coordinator); credit is assigned by four ablation conditions over 720 runs.
Contribution is auto-synthesising the code harness that blocks illegal actions before execution, i.e. how the gate is produced; validated on 145 TextArena games in the lab.
Contribution is MCP as a strict pre-execution validation boundary intercepting malformed tool calls; empirical evaluation over four datasets with ablations, no deployment.
Contribution is a measurement procedure -- verifiable Python task chains scoring long-horizon depth and one self-correction attempt -- and it is used to score ten models in the lab.

Contributes a functional-property framework and recurring failure patterns across agent architectures rather than one mechanism; five capability augmentations are added and compared to attribute effects.
Contribution is reflective global replanning plus action-space expansion deciding the next step after a failure; validated against baselines on the released ToolHop-Pro benchmark.
Contribution is a deterministic DAG engine that owns routing, state transitions and conditional control flow instead of prompted orchestration; evaluated on GAIA against six frameworks.
Contribution is a six-verb tool-interaction protocol with next-action metadata fixing the phases of the loop; measured on 50 real operational tasks in a live production SaaS platform.

Its formalized mechanism is adaptive timeout-budget allocation across sequential tool calls (identity gating the runner-up); mechanisms are only stated as testable hypotheses backed by deployment vignettes.
Contribution is automatically constructing the agent DAG, roles and I/O contracts from a task description and dispatching across it; benchmarked against multi-agent baselines with ablations.
Contribution is a Petri-net control plane enforcing retry budgets that guarantee termination and cap regeneration cost; evidence is 200 controlled generation cycles comparing two recovery strategies.
Contributes an ATT&CK-anchored evaluation of agent loop behaviour with failure attribution rather than a mechanism; three operational modalities compared in a controlled emulation range.
Contribution is process-level behavioural measurement (retries, reflection, memory use, recovery) of agentic components; fixed workflow and reflective variants compared under one harness.
Headline artefact is a 1,000-task MCP benchmark with claim-level scoring and a failure taxonomy; used to score 20 frontier models in the lab.
Contribution is an FSM of app navigation whose stored state drives planning, verification and recovery to an earlier state, not window fitting; validated on Mobile-Eval-E, SPA-Bench, AndroidWorld.
Contribution is deterministic graph routing that decides the next tool step and reroutes on failure without the LLM; evidence is 19 scenarios over three topologies against ReAct and static baselines.
Headline artefact is a white-box trace-level benchmark suite for agentic systems; 21 system variants measured with it in the lab.
